display.name: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL - CloudWatch
display.description: Cluster and instance health for Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, from AWS/RDS CloudWatch metrics scraped with the Prometheus CloudWatch Exporter. Instance panels are scoped by dbinstance_identifier so writer and reader appear as separate series; storage-volume and serverless-capacity panels are cluster-scoped. Engine internals (buffers, vacuum, locks, index usage) live in the companion Aurora PostgreSQL engine-metrics dashboard.

display.name: dbcluster_identifier
display.description: Aurora DB cluster identifier. Scopes the cluster-level panels (storage volume, serverless capacity).

display.name: dbinstance_identifier
display.description: Aurora DB instance identifier, one value per writer and reader instance. Scopes the per-instance panels.

display.name: Serverless Database Capacity
display.description: Aurora Capacity Units provisioned for the cluster. Serverless v2 only.

display.name: ACU Utilization
display.description: Share of the instance's maximum ACU setting in use. Sustained values near 100% mean the max capacity setting is the ceiling.

display.name: CPU Utilization
display.description: CPU used by the database engine on each instance.

display.name: Database Connections
display.description: Client connections open on each instance.

display.name: Aurora Replica Lag
display.description: Lag between a reader and the writer over the shared storage volume. Reported by reader instances only, so the writer has no series here.

display.name: Engine Uptime
display.description: Time since the engine last started. A drop marks a restart or failover.

display.name: Freeable Memory
display.description: RAM available on each instance.

display.name: Buffer Cache Hit Ratio
display.description: Share of requests served from the buffer cache. A sustained drop means the working set no longer fits in memory.

display.name: Swap Usage
display.description: Swap space used on the instance. Anything above zero for long is memory pressure.

display.name: Commit Latency
display.description: Average time to commit a transaction.

display.name: Commit Throughput
display.description: Commits per second, split by writer and reader role on the cluster.

display.name: Deadlocks
display.description: Deadlocks per second detected by the engine.

display.name: Maximum Used Transaction IDs
display.description: Age of the oldest unfrozen transaction ID. Growth towards 2 billion means autovacuum is falling behind and wraparound protection will stop writes.

display.name: Instance IOPS
display.description: Read and write I/O operations per second on the instance's local storage.

display.name: Instance I/O Latency
display.description: Average time per read and write I/O operation on local storage.

display.name: Instance I/O Throughput
display.description: Bytes read from and written to local storage per second.

display.name: Disk Queue Depth
display.description: Outstanding I/O requests waiting to access the disk.

display.name: Network Throughput
display.description: Client network traffic to and from the instance. Storage traffic to the cluster volume is not counted here.

display.name: Volume Bytes Used
display.description: Storage consumed by the cluster volume. CloudWatch emits this at 5-minute intervals, and it takes about an hour to appear on a new cluster.

display.name: Volume Read I/O Operations (5 min)
display.description: Billed read operations against the cluster volume. CloudWatch reports this as a count of billed operations per 5-minute interval, not a rate. Divide by 300 for operations per second.

display.name: Volume Write I/O Operations (5 min)
display.description: Billed write operations against the cluster volume. CloudWatch reports this as a count of billed operations per 5-minute interval, not a rate. Divide by 300 for operations per second.

display.name: Transaction Logs Disk Usage
display.description: Disk consumed by write-ahead logs. Aurora PostgreSQL uses log records instead of transaction logs unless logical replication or AWS DMS is active, and reports -1 while they are unused. A flat -1 line is expected on a cluster with neither.

display.name: Replication Slot Disk Usage
display.description: Disk held by replication slots. Grows without bound when a logical subscriber stops consuming. Reads 0 on a cluster with no logical replication slots.

display.name: Oldest Replication Slot Lag
display.description: WAL retained for the furthest-behind replica or logical slot.
